match.reason: No existing point covers globalisation's effect on operations, meaning global sourcing, production anywhere and worldwide competition; the closest ones are only about where a business operates or about general external influences.

draft.title: Globalisation and operations
card: Globalisation is the growing links between countries through trade, investment, technology and the movement of people and information. Markets become global, not just local.
Businesses can source inputs, such as materials, parts and labour, from any country. They can also choose to make goods or deliver services in any country.
Operations managers can choose the place that best suits their goals. Low labour costs, skilled workers or nearby suppliers may each be the deciding reason.
Globalisation also brings competition from around the world. Overseas firms can sell into the local market, so a business must compete on price, quality and delivery.
draft.remember: Globalisation widens where operations can buy and make, and who they compete against.

a.q: Which change in operations is a direct result of globalisation?
opts: A firm buys parts from the cheapest supplier in any country
A firm hires more staff because local demand has grown
A firm installs a new machine to cut errors on its line
A firm follows a new local law on safe work practices
a.why: Globalisation lets a firm source inputs from any country, so it can choose the cheapest supplier abroad. Installing a machine is a technology choice, and local law is government regulation, so neither is the effect of global markets.
a.clue: Which choice relies on suppliers being open to buyers in other countries?

b.q: Priya runs a furniture factory in Newcastle. Cheaper imported furniture now fills Australian shops and her sales have dropped. Which is the best explanation?
opts: Global markets bring overseas rivals into her local market
Her factory has lost the right to source timber from abroad
Local customers now care less about the quality of furniture
Her suppliers have raised prices because of local demand
b.why: Globalisation lets overseas firms sell into Australian markets, so Priya now competes with imports on price. Nothing in the case says customers care less about quality, and the drop in sales comes from competition, not from her suppliers.
b.clue: Think about who else can now sell furniture to her customers.

a.best: A firm buys parts from the cheapest supplier in any country

b.best: Global markets bring overseas rivals into her local market
